$$y = \frac{3x-1}{x+2} \qquad x>-2$$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a)  Show that
$$\frac{3x-1}{x+2}\equiv A+\frac{B}{x+2}$$
where $A$ and $B$ are constants to be found.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Obtains either $A=3$ or $B=-7$
A1: $3-\frac{7}{x+2}$. Just stating the values of $A$ and $B$ is insufficient but this may be awarded if seen in (b). Allow $3+\frac{-7}{x+2}$ and $3+-\frac{7}{x+2}$
Official notes (completeness pass):

parts.text:
The finite region $R$, shown shaded in Figure 4, is bounded by the curve, the line with
equation $x=4$, the $x$-axis and the line with equation $x=1$
This region is rotated through $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis to form a solid of revolution.

(b)  Use the answer to part (a) and algebraic integration to find the exact volume of the
solid generated, giving your answer in the form
$$\pi(p+q\ln2)$$
where $p$ and $q$ are rational constants.
(6)
